module: "Start and drive off" tutorial of the First Drive experience. Once enabled, it follows player 0's vehicle (throttle, brake, clutch, gear, engine, RPM, wheel speed, read via core_vehicleBridge) and shows in the "moveOff" application of the "topCenter" container the keys to use for each step: turn the engine on, drive off, stop, reverse, turn the engine off. The instructions depend on the gearbox mode: arcade, realistic manual with automatic clutch, or realistic manual.
usage:
ui_firstDrive_moveOff.setEnabled(true)
-- the interface receives the FirstDriveMoveOffState event on each instruction change
local state = ui_firstDrive_moveOff.getState()
notes: UI event: FirstDriveMoveOffState, with { label, steps, sectionIndex, sectionCount, active }. Each step contains action, actionLabel, inputType ("press", "hold" or "release"), status ("complete", "current" or "upcoming") and possibly separator ("or"). On deactivation, { active = false } is sent.
The number of sections is 5 in arcade and in automatic clutch, 6 in realistic manual (extra step to shift to neutral before driving off).
The hook onFirstDriveMoveOffSectionCompleted is emitted (once, with the section name: engineOn, moveOff, stopping, reverse or engineOff) after the state update that completed the section.

Thresholds used: wheel speed 0.5 m/s for "moving", 1.5 m/s to validate reversing, 1500 RPM before releasing the clutch, brake 0.2, clutch held from 0.8 and released below 0.15. A 2 s pause separates each section and 0.3 s is waited after each vehicle change to let the values refresh.

The mode (arcade, realisticAutoClutch, realisticManual) is determined by the gearboxMode value of the vehicle's mainController (fallback: setting defaultGearboxBehavior, "arcade"), then by the autoClutch setting.
The extension disables itself on onExtensionUnloaded and onClientEndMission; a settings change restarts the vehicle tracking after 0.1 s.
Only player 0 is tracked: onVehicleSwitched ignores the other players.

dependencies.desc: Extensions loaded before this one: ui_appContainers.

setEnabled.desc: Enables or disables the tutorial. On enable, starts following player 0's vehicle (subscriptions to the values throttle_input, brake_input, clutch_input, gearIndex, engineRunning, rpm, wheelspeed); on disable, unsubscribes, hides the application and sends { active = false }. No effect if the state does not change.

value.desc: Only true enables; any other value disables.

getEnabled.desc: Indicates whether the tutorial is active.

getState.desc: Returns the last published instruction (label, steps, sectionIndex, sectionCount, active), or nil if nothing is displayed.

returns.desc: Last state sent to the interface.

onUpdate.desc: Hook called every frame with dtReal (real seconds). Reconfigures the tracking if the player's vehicle changes, waits for the delays to end, computes the current instruction, publishes it to the interface if it has changed and emits onFirstDriveMoveOffSectionCompleted when a section has just been validated.

onVehicleSwitched.desc: Hook called when the player's vehicle changes. Restarts the tracking on the new vehicle (ignored if inactive or if player is not 0).

_.desc: Identifier of the old vehicle (not used).

onVehicleDestroyed.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is destroyed: stops the tracking if it is the tracked vehicle.

onVehicleReplaced.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is replaced; same handling as onVehicleDestroyed.

onSettingsChanged.desc: Hook called when the settings change. If active, restarts the vehicle tracking after 0.1 s, which rereads the gearbox mode.

onExtensionUnloaded.desc: Hook called when the extension is unloaded: disables the tutorial.

onClientEndMission.desc: Hook called at the end of the level: disables the tutorial.
